evals.prompt: Write a short tutorial that teaches a new user to run the project, then link to separate reference documentation.
assertions: The response treats the artifact as a tutorial
The tutorial leads to a working result rather than listing every option
Reference material is separated or linked

evals.prompt: Update the README with the real install command, CLI flags, and expected output from this repository.
assertions: The response inspects repository source/configuration before claiming commands
Examples use exact commands and realistic expected output
Inline expected output is a single #-prefixed comment value so command blocks remain copy-pasteable
Unverified claims are marked or omitted

evals.prompt: Make this GitHub README easier to scan without adding marketing language.
assertions: The response preserves a logical heading hierarchy
The response uses concise sections, lists, and purposeful callouts
The response avoids decorative or unsupported content

evals.prompt: Document this API endpoint for users, including inputs, outputs, errors, side effects, and one edge case.
assertions: The response documents the public contract rather than implementation details
Errors and side effects are included
The example is grounded in the actual API

evals.prompt: Add documentation tests for a repository whose Python examples live in Markdown, including a beginner API guard and an expert-only allowlist.
assertions: The response proposes executing marked doctest fences
The response adds policy tests for canonical vocabulary or forbidden legacy forms
The response keeps expert-only exceptions narrow and explicit
The response wires focused docs tests into the repository check and CI path filters
